::: proof
The weighted residual sum of squares for a constant $a$ is
$Q(a) \eqdef \sum_{i=1}^n w_i (y_i - a)^2$.
Its derivative is

$$
\ba
Q'(a)
&= \sum_{i=1}^n w_i \cdot 2 (y_i - a) \cdot (-1)
&& \text{(chain rule, term by term)}
\\ &= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{-2 w_i y_i + 2 a w_i}
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\ &= -2 \sum_{i=1}^n w_i y_i + 2 a \sum_{i=1}^n w_i
&& \text{(split the sum)}
\ea
$$

Setting $Q'(a) = 0$:

$$
\ba
2 a \sum_{i=1}^n w_i &= 2 \sum_{i=1}^n w_i y_i
&& \text{(add } 2 \textstyle\sum w_i y_i \text{ to both sides)}
\\ a &= \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n w_i y_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n w_i}
&& \text{(divide by } 2 \textstyle\sum w_i > 0\text{)}
\ea
$$

The second derivative $Q''(a) = 2\sum_{i=1}^n w_i$ is positive,
so this stationary point is the minimizer.
:::
